rule.statement: A Divisional Secretary does not have the statutory power to place a person in possession and occupation of State land before the due execution of an instrument of lease under the State Lands Ordinance.
rule.supporting_quote: The aforesaid question cannot be decided here since it does not arise for determination in this appeal which has been decided on the limited ground that the Divisional Secretary did not have the statutory power to place the 2nd respondent in possession and occupation of the land before the due execution of an instrument of lease under the provisions of the State Lands Ordinance.
